name: Spicy Sticky Lamb Chops
ingredients: 1 tsp - hot sauce, such as sriracha
As Needed - Freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Place coriander and fennel seeds in a small frying pan over medium heat. Toast, shaking  the pan every 30 seconds or so, until fragrant and slightly darker in color, about 2  minutes. Transfer to a small bowl and let cool completely.

Meanwhile, peel and finely grate a 2-inch piece of ginger until you have 4 teaspoons.  Mince 5-6 garlic cloves until you have 4 teaspoons. Place both in a medium bowl. Add 1/4 cup plain yogurt, 1/4 cup tomato paste, 4 teaspoons vegetable oil, 2 teaspoons packed  light brown sugar, 2 teaspoons kosher salt, 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon  hot sauce, and a few grinds of black pepper. Stir to combine.

Transfer the toasted coriander and fennel into a spice grinder or mortar and grind into a  fine powder. Add the spices to the yogurt mixture and stir to combine. Taste and season  with more salt as needed.

Dip and coat 8 bone-in lamb loin chops one at a time in the yogurt mixture, rubbing it  into the meat and fat. Place the lamb chops in a plastic bag or airtight container.  Refrigerate at least 30 minutes or up to overnight.

Arrange a rack in the middle of the oven and heat the oven to 475˚F. 6. Transfer the lamb chops to a 9x13-inch baking dish, arranging them in a single layer.  Bake until the thickest part of the lamb chop registers 145˚F on an instant-read  thermometer for medium-rare, 15-20 minutes. Remove from the oven. Loosely cover  the baking dish with aluminum foil and let the lamb rest for 5 minutes before serving. Storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

additional_context.source: This is a spicy creamy middle eastern dish. From thekitchn.com and adaped by the Rocking M Farm
